label: rem:negative-debt-confinement
title: Negative coefficient debt, confinement, and the nine-strand direction
html:
The NF_+ / NF_- decomposition of the nucleon normal forms reveals a quantitative signature of confinement. The neutron carries significantly more internal cancellation than the proton.

The topological-deficit

Each nucleon's Gröbner--Shirshov normal form splits into positive and negative coefficient sums. The neutron's topological-deficit |\mathrm{NF}_-(\mathfrak{n})| = 0.2555 exceeds the proton's by |\Delta\mathrm{NF}_-| = 0.1127. This excess deficit is 11.3\% of the proton's net coefficient.

The dominant source is the L_+ sign flip. This single channel contributes approximately the entire excess deficit.

Confinement interpretation

The internal cancellation ratio measures how much of the total coefficient magnitude is consumed by destructive interference:

  • Neutron: 19.3\% cancellation
  • Proton: 11.1\% cancellation

The neutron's larger cancellation reflects its composition. The d--d crossing generates a correction that propagates through the reduction. It flips the L_+ coefficient and amplifies the \gamma debt. This is a computable, algebraic manifestation of color confinement. The energy cost of holding three quarks in a color-singlet braid is larger for the neutron because the d--d interaction is more confining than u--u.
